::: {.lead-in}
Companion field guide for a two-hour session at the CRT Annual Training Conference 2026, for Wisconsin Cyber Response Team volunteers and fellow SLTT IT professionals.
:::

The live session is a focused presentation. This site holds what does not fit in two hours: calculators, sample files, commands you can copy, scripts, longer explanations and the primary sources behind each claim.

The five topics were assigned and are somewhat disparate. Their connection is practical security knowledge CRT responders should understand and be able to explain, including preventative advice that helps organizations avoid the incidents we respond to.

## Topics

::: {.topic-grid}
::: {.topic-card}
### [1. Passwords](passwords.qmd)
How passwords get guessed, what an entropy model can tell us, and what infrastructure should do to protect users.

Entropy calculator · cracking time and cost explorer · NIST SP 800-63B-4
:::

::: {.topic-card}
### [2. PKI](pki.qmd)
Inspect a certificate, explain issuance, and name the validation check that fails.

Sample certificates · field reference · OpenSSL and certutil · AD CS and ACME
:::

::: {.topic-card}
### [3. Email security](email.qmd)
How email moves, which identities are authenticated, and whether a message passes DMARC.

Header walkthroughs · alignment checker · SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS records
:::

::: {.topic-card}
### [4. PowerShell](powershell.qmd)
Make administrative and incident-response tasks easier to repeat and automate.

Copyable examples · file inventory and EVTX scripts · 5.1 versus 7
:::

::: {.topic-card}
### [5. Windows DFIR box](dfir.qmd)
Build a repeatable Windows workstation for analyzing evidence that has already been collected.

Build scripts · reset and retention checks · open decisions
:::
:::

## How to read this site

- Commands and scripts were run against the sample files before publishing; outputs shown are real, sometimes trimmed. Versions are noted where behavior varies.
- Each section cites its primary sources inline. The [references](references.qmd) page collects them.
- Where something is a proposal, an assumption or an open decision rather than settled guidance, it is labeled that way.
